[duplicate/medium] R103, R104: Both require reporting the percentage of checkouts at a library location that are renewals. R103 includes this same location-level rate in addition to its separate item-level renewal-likelihood estimate.
[duplicate/medium] R110, R111: Both require administrators to restrict template edits, specifically preventing edits that expose deleted items while allowing safe changes such as call-number ranges.
[duplicate/medium] R092, R094, R095: R092 already requires reports for long call numbers and bibliographic records without associated items; R094 and R095 separately restate those same report needs.

[duplicate/medium] R045, R046: Both require audit records of deletions/purges identifying who performed the action and when. R046 additionally specifies broader deletion details and reporting, but the purge-audit need overlaps.
[conflict/high] R077, R231: R077 makes badge-swipe login an alternative to username/password authentication, while R231 says cards must not replace individual authentication.

[conflict/high] R048, R215: R048 permits filtering patron records by demographic criteria, while R215 requires null and blank fields to be included regardless of filtering. A filter that excludes null-valued records cannot satisfy both requirements.

[out_of_scope/medium] R123: Updating fines, charges, and waivers makes the reporting system responsible for changing operational financial records, rather than reading and analyzing enterprise data as scoped.
[out_of_scope/medium] R177, R179: These requirements cover collecting or reporting voter and voter-registration survey responses, which is unrelated to the stated library management reporting scope.

[unclear/medium] R247, R248: These describe organizational responsibilities—supervising a unit and directing library services—rather than capabilities the reporting system can provide. The descriptions only identify report access or use as a possible support.

[inconsistent_vocabulary/medium] R040, R141, R149, R021, R256: These use glossary synonyms instead of the preferred terms: “branch” for Library location, “borrower” for Patron, “system-wide” for Consortium, and “public catalog” for Online Public Access Catalog.

[wrong_priority/medium] R182, R183: Both are Must solely because their statements use “shall.” The priority scale reserves Must for essential, mandated, or core-purpose requirements; the rationales do not establish that these specialized reports meet that threshold.

[duplicate/medium] R001, R002: R002 repeats R001’s requirement that the Material Volume Report use new acquisitions, on-shelf items, and items out in circulation as its data sources.
[duplicate/medium] R048, R049, R215: These requirements repeat the need to include null or blank values in report results; R049 narrows the same behavior to patron fields.

[conflict/high] R048, R203, R215: R048 and R215 require null and blank fields to appear regardless of display choices, while R203 lets users select which data elements to include. The requirements do not reconcile whether a user may omit a field.

[duplicate/medium] R076, R108: Both require optional streamlined staff login methods alongside individual credential login; R108 gives badge swipe as an example of the capability described more generally in R076.
[duplicate/medium] R077, R231: Both require that streamlined or card-based login must not bypass individual staff authentication.
[duplicate/medium] R129, R149: Both require an overdue-items report using a specified days-overdue threshold and including information for patron follow-up.
[duplicate/medium] R150, R157: Both require a report listing items classified as long overdue.
[duplicate/medium] R188, R190: Both require reports of inter-library loans by Library location from the Reporting warehouse for operational review.

[out_of_scope/high] R042, R044: These requirements directly change item statuses or delete item and volume records. Those are source-record management actions, whereas the product scope is a reporting and analysis system and excludes management of core cataloging and circulation workflows.
[out_of_scope/high] R226: Updating financial information when a patron pays at a staff desk is a transactional workflow, not read-only reporting and analysis.
[inconsistent_vocabulary/medium] R065, R074, R075, R086, R232, R248: These requirements use “system-wide,” which the glossary lists as a synonym to avoid for Consortium.
[inconsistent_vocabulary/medium] R072: “Branch-level” uses a glossary-listed synonym for Library location.
[inconsistent_vocabulary/medium] R079: “Predefined reports” uses a glossary-listed synonym for Canned report.
[inconsistent_vocabulary/medium] R132, R194: “Non-Cataloged material” and “non-cataloged collections” use glossary-listed synonyms for Uncataloged material.

[inconsistent_vocabulary/medium] R232, R251: These requirements use “Global System Administrator” or “Local System Administrator,” which the glossary lists as synonyms to avoid for Global administrator and Local administrator.

[duplicate/medium] R001, R004: R001 already requires configurable categories in the Material Volume Report and hold counts by category. R004 restates those same capabilities.
[duplicate/medium] R001, R008: R001 already requires the report to show the number of holds as a distinct breakdown; R008 restates that reporting need.

[duplicate/medium] R133, R134: Both require a combined total circulation report covering cataloged and uncataloged material. R133 adds a type breakdown, but R134's core combined-report need is already covered.
[duplicate/high] R153, R221: Both require a report of deleted items that were the last copy, including the affected library location. These express the same reporting need.

[unclear/medium] R048: Requiring patron records with null or blank optional values to appear regardless of filtering makes it unclear how demographic and activity filters are meant to apply; null-valued records could bypass the selected criteria.

[unclear/medium] R246: “Create report content and design services reflected in reports” does not clearly state whether staff design reports or design library services, so the requirement does not match its name unambiguously.

[out_of_scope/medium] R241: The requirement extends beyond reporting and data-quality analysis to grouped or automated changes across item, bibliographic, volume, and patron records. This describes broad operational record modification rather than the stated reporting-system scope.

[wrong_priority/medium] R009: The rationale cites “need/should” language, but assigns Must by treating that wording as essential. The explicit “should” cue aligns with Should on the stated priority scale, absent a stronger mandatory cue.
